findings.claim: 1. gauntlet-design.md:121 ("`$INPUTS.<name>` appears only in prompts and `bash:` bodies") binds write/ and mend/ through :123 ("follow the same rules") and the Homes row at :341 ("`$INPUTS.<name>` in prompts and `bash:`; `INPUTS_<NAME>` in scripts"). The writing and landing designs put `$INPUTS.<name>` in `with:` bindings: writing-design.md:492 ("`<slug>` ... in prompts and `with:` come from `$INPUTS.slug`", used at :434 and :441) and landing-design.md:73, :91, :155 (`brief: $INPUTS.brief`). Rows: A3/A14; the contract a missing row would hold is 'where `$INPUTS` may appear inside a phase block' (gauntlet-design.md:341).
findings.failure_scenario: A builder who follows gauntlet-design.md must rewrite the `screen` and `flag` bindings of write/ and the `red`, `confirm` and `recheck` bindings of mend/, which the phase designs give verbatim. A builder who follows the phase designs breaks gauntlet-design.md's home rule. Whichever the builder picks, one design is broken, and the reviewer of the other design files a defect against the built file.

findings.claim: 2. gauntlet-design.md:290 ("True when run timed out; or a test FAILED or ERROR in run is failing in neither brief nor head") makes a timeout red unconditionally. A timeout already present in the brief baseline, or on the checkout's HEAD alone, still counts as red, although :292 exempts failures already present in brief or head. Row: S4 (internal to the red rule).
findings.failure_scenario: Case 1: the brief baseline timed out at the cut. Every writing test run is then red, the juror is called on every cut, and the run can reach `stalled` or DEFECTIVE over a condition the writers did not cause. Case 2: the owner's new checkout commits make the suite hang. The mend's `confirm` is red even though `test-head` timed out the same way, so `repair` opens and the owner is asked about a red the tree did not cause (CLAUDE.md 1.4).

findings.claim: 3. gauntlet-design.md:348 ("hidden from every other checkout role by `FENCE_HIDE=gauntlet/failed`") and :355 ("Refusing a read inside a readable folder | `FENCE_HIDE`") do not hold for spec review. Node `file` holds `allowed_tools: [Task, Bash]` (spec-review-design.md:359) and its `spiker` holds `Bash` (:370). Their sandbox limits writes only (:361), and FENCE_HIDE covers fence tools only. Row: F4 (also P10).
findings.failure_scenario: A slug has a record under the checkout's gauntlet/failed/. During spec review, the speccer, or a spiker it dispatches, runs `cat gauntlet/failed/<slug>.txt` through Bash. The read succeeds, and the 'no other role reads it' home is breached, while `speccer.mcp.json`'s FENCE_HIDE gives the appearance of confinement.

findings.claim: 4. gauntlet-design.md:247 ("then each `gauntlet/revisions/<slug>-summary.<N>.md` in order of N") and :350 ("each revision summary in order of N") put every revision summary in the final commit message. The reporter writes a summary for every SOUND round (writing-design.md:89, :219), including rounds the owner then sends back with `revise` (writing-design.md:494, "the owner revises a SOUND revision"). Row: H33.
findings.failure_scenario: Round 1 is SOUND, so the reporter writes `<slug>-summary.1.md`. The owner chooses revise. Round 2 is SOUND and the owner approves it, so only round 2 becomes `.rev1.txt`. `seal` still lists summary 1 and summary 2 in `<slug>: final`. The commit landing shows at its gate therefore describes a revision that was never entered.

findings.claim: 5. gauntlet-design.md:19 ("The run ends at block `land` ..., after `cut` ..., and at node `kill`, cancelled ...") and :98 omit the `vacate` cancel inside writing (writing-design.md:353-356, `cancel: "... The run stops."`). That node cancels the tree run, not gauntlet-run. This design does not say what node `tree`, `cut`, `fail` or `kill` do when the child run ends cancelled. The `vacate` nodes of plan review and spec review are also missing from the list. Rows: H25 and A18 (also H18).
findings.failure_scenario: Twelve revision verdicts of OBJECTION: LEADING retire every reviewer slot, and `vacate` cancels gauntlet-tree. Its `handoff` never runs, so `cut` has no `$tree.output` to read. gauntlet-run then ends by an undefined route: node `tree` failed (treated by :98 as a resumable "failed phase", which reruns writing straight back into `vacate`) or cancelled. In neither case does the design say what the owner sees or does.

findings.claim: 6. The copy list at gauntlet-design.md:23-34 states, as current fact, copies that the other designs (and this design's own modules) no longer hold. :23 says each phase description "invites direct use"; intake:137, plan-review:244 and spec-review:298 say "Not for direct use" (H13-H15). :24 says `worktree: enabled: false` sits in the three phase files; intake:221, plan-review:239 and spec-review:293 declare none (A1). :25 says the checkout holds 3 guard nodes; plan-review:12, spec-review:293 and intake:221 hold none (H1, S13). :26 says "Plan review's and spec review's declare none" (no output_format); plan-review:406 and spec-review:460-463 declare one (H4, H5). :27 places `$INPUTS` left of `when:` on intake's `from-file` and `ground`; intake:157 and :164 read `$route.output.file` (H6, A2). :28 counts 2 inline handoffs; spec-review:456 uses the named `handoff.ts` (A3). :29, :32, :33 and :34 name needs that this design's own :228, writing:19, :279 and landing:256 now meet (H8, R12, S4, H12).
findings.failure_scenario: Every builder and reviewer who loads gauntlet-design.md reads 12 bullets about the current state of other designs, and about 10 of them are false. Plan 2's own contracts seed rows from these bullets (contracts.md:9). A reader who trusts :26 expects no output_format on plan review's `handoff`, which contradicts H4 and wastes the reader's tokens checking the claim (CLAUDE.md 1.3).

findings.claim: 7. gauntlet-design.md:247 ("Node `seal` is the writing design's, with one change: it commits with `git commit -F -`") and build step :371 (`write/write.yaml (node seal), write/fixtures/written.stubs.yaml`) restate work the writing design already does. writing-design.md:408-410 already commits with `git commit -F -` and the same message, and writing:494 and :541 already build the sealed `written` fixture. Row: H33.
findings.failure_scenario: Step 9 runs after writing:7 and finds `seal` and the sealed fixture already as specified. It spends a `workflow-builder` dispatch and a validate cycle to change nothing, or it rewrites a correct node (CLAUDE.md 1.3).

findings.claim: 8. gauntlet-design.md:243 ("Each holds only its revision: the clauses it changes, each as it now reads") conflicts with :229. There `enter` does `cp -n` of the approved round file, and writing-design.md:31 gives that file the lines `Revises: plan|spec` and `Answers: <tree path>` before the clauses. Writing:344 confirms that `enter` copies the round file $record.output.enter. Row: P3.
findings.failure_scenario: `.rev1.txt` carries the `Revises:` and `Answers: gauntlet/write/<slug>.verdict.N.txt` lines. The rule "the approved plan is `<slug>.txt` with every revision applied" then hands agents a header that is not plan text, and that header points at a tree file the mend's agents and the checkout record may not carry.

findings.claim: 9. gauntlet-design.md:184 ("Its only agent nodes are `mend-juror`, `mend-code`, `mend-tests` and `mend-review`") names node ids that the landing design does not use. In landing-design.md:109-112 and :157-159 the nodes are `juror` and `review`, with `command: mend-juror` and `command: mend-review`. Row: H34.
findings.failure_scenario: A builder or fixture author who keys gauntlet-tree's mend stubs, or a check of 'only these agent nodes', on gauntlet-design.md's ids finds no `mend-juror` or `mend-review` node in mend/mend.yaml. The stub does not match, or the check flags the landing design's own ids.
